q1_issues.issue: "PacifiCats" is a proper noun (a named class of vessels) but no Name fact is emitted for it — the surface string is lost, leaving only the lowercase kind symbol pacificat, and the instruction set states that neither the name-derived symbol nor its Name atom is optional.

q2_gaps: a PLURAL proper noun naming a class of manufactured things ("the PacifiCats") — a singular proper noun (one symbol + one Name) and a definite plural (group witness + GroupOf kind) are each covered, but not their combination: nothing says whether the Name attaches to the group witness or to the kind symbol minted from the name
notes: The rest follows the instruction set: the coordinated by-phrase splits distributively into two design events sharing one patient, the passive by-phrases take Agent, Patient is right for a creation verb, and the two entity-attached origin/affiliation phrases keep their own surface prepositions, (From philip_hercus vancouver) and (Of robert_allan_limited australia). That one relation lands on two heads is what the never-a-synonym-head rule requires, not a defect.
